The Writing Studio · Chapter 2 · AssessmentCase 01 — Beyond the Headline

Communications wants to publish a story saying the online workshop from Chapter 1 was a major success. Before it goes out, you check whether each claim in the draft is supported by the records. Complete the five steps below, in order. About 20–30 minutes; your work is saved in this browser.

  1. 1
    Computer · First readingRead the draft publication (D01). Answer the 3 first-reading questions, then press Record first reading. This unlocks the rest of the case. These three answers are frozen once recorded.
  2. 2
    Case file and phone · InvestigateOpen the case file and read all three tabs: D02 (attendance and survey), D03 (infographic) and D04 (internal email). Then open the phone and read the participant messages (D05).
  3. 3
    Computer · Critical analysisAnswer the 10 questions in the Critical analysis tab. Go back to the documents whenever you need to; answers save automatically.
  4. 4
    Evidence board · Connect and judgeThe board has 6 yellow claims (C) and 6 blue evidence notes (E). For every claim: connect it to at least one evidence note that justifies your judgment (click its pin, then another pin, or drag a thread from pin to pin), and classify it: press and hold the yellow note (or right-click it) and choose supported, partially supported, insufficient evidence or contradicted. Click a thread to remove it. Moving notes and writing on the green pad in the corner are optional and not graded.
  5. 5
    Notebook · Decide and submitChoose a recommendation (publish, revise, or hold until more evidence is available) and write an analytical report of at least 60 words in your own words, using the evidence you found. Then press Submit.

How it is assessed. Steps 1–4 are scored automatically (85 points). Your report is reviewed by your instructor (15 points). Feedback and correct answers appear only after you submit, and your first submission is final. You can then export your record.

Getting around. Select an object in the office to open it; Back to desk or Escape returns to your seat. The bar at the top of the computer shows which steps are complete, and the notebook tells you what is still missing.
